Proportional abundance

Source: R/proportional.abundance.R
proportional.abundance.Rd

Computes the proportional abundance of every sample: the abundance of every element in the sample, divided by a reference level of that element across all samples, added up over the elements. The reference level of an element is a percentile of its nonzero abundances in all samples, so every element is measured on its own scale and abundant elements do not dominate the index.

Usage

proportional.abundance(abund, percentile = 100, cap_at = NULL)

Arguments

abund

Numeric matrix, data.frame or sparse Matrix of abundances with samples in rows and elements (units or subunits) in columns. Column names are the element identifiers.

percentile

Single number in (0, 100] (default 100, the maximum). Percentile of the nonzero abundances of every element across the samples used as its reference level.

cap_at

NULL (default) or a single positive number. If NULL, the ratios are not capped. Otherwise, every element's ratio higher than cap_at is set to cap_at. With percentile = 100 every ratio is at most 1, so only a cap_at below 1 changes the result.

Value

Named numeric vector with the proportional abundance of every sample. Samples with zero total abundance get 0.

Details

The function does not know whether the columns of abund are units or subunits: it treats every column as one element.

Let \(x_{ij}\) be the abundance of element \(j\) in sample \(i\), and \(P_j\) the percentile (type 7 quantile, see stats::quantile()) of its nonzero abundances across samples. Then $$PA_i = \sum_{j \,:\, x_{ij} > 0} \frac{x_{ij}}{P_j},$$ or, with a numeric cap_at \(c\), $$PA_i = \sum_{j \,:\, x_{ij} > 0} \min\left(\frac{x_{ij}}{P_j}, c\right).$$

With percentile = 100, \(P_j\) is the maximum abundance of the element, every ratio is in (0, 1] and the index is at most the number of elements present. Elements absent from all samples have no reference level and contribute 0. The index does not change if all abundances are multiplied by the same constant.

See also

proportional.abundance.ref_abu() when the reference abundances are known, multiplicity.inventory(), relative.multiplicity()

Examples

abund <- matrix(
  c(10, 0, 4, 6,
    5,  8, 3, 0,
    0, 12, 7, 9),
  nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE,
  dimnames = list(c("S1", "S2", "S3"), c("e1", "e2", "e3", "e4"))
)

proportional.abundance(abund)
#>       S1       S2       S3 
#> 2.238095 1.595238 3.000000 
proportional.abundance(abund, percentile = 50)
#>       S1       S2       S3 
#> 3.133333 2.216667 4.150000 
proportional.abundance(abund, percentile = 50, cap_at = 1)
#>       S1       S2       S3 
#> 2.800000 2.216667 3.000000
